label: sec:m4_objectives
claim: Huber uses delta_h = 1.345 after scaling each series by the standard deviation of its differenced values; in the controlled study Huber is warm-started from the MSE fit; the ridge objective uses lambda = sqrt(max(n_eff, 1)) without the Gaussian MA normalization.
evidence: Source at 14dd581, src/models/sarima.jl: DEFAULT_HUBER_DELTA = 1.345 on yValues ./ std(differenced series); `objectiveFunction == "huber" && isnothing(warmStart)` starts from MSE; lambda = sqrt(max(nEff, 1)) in the ridge branch, which carries no determinant factor.

label: sec:initialization_likelihood
claim: Under :innovations the Gaussian quadratic criterion uses the factorized MA normalization D_reg(theta) D_seas(Theta); for mixed multiplicative MA models it omits the regular-seasonal resultant correction of the complete stationary-history factor D_reg D_seas [R(theta, Theta; s)^2]^(-1/T), which Supplementary Section S2 derives.
evidence: src/models/sarima.jl, MA block of the :penalized/:innovations MSE objective: the factor is prod_j (1 - kappa_j^2)^(-j/T) times prod_w (1 - kappa_w^2)^(-s w/T), with no resultant term, at 14dd581, aa68d57, 3d7f883 and 21903b5. Measured on the package (verification/ma_normalization/package_factor.jl, at 14dd581 and 21903b5): the factor applied equals D_reg D_seas to eight decimals. The supplement's complete factor is exact (verification/ma_normalization/check_ma_normalization.py, to 4e-14 in log); the omitted factor lies between 0.987 and 1.010 at T = 200 over random invertible draws. Known defect of the implementation, not changed (LIMITATIONS.md, item 22).

label: sec:initialization_likelihood
claim: For additive seasonal models the implementation likewise does not evaluate the determinant of the complete MA polynomial 1 + sum theta_j B^j + sum Theta_w B^(sw).
evidence: The package applies the same separate regular and seasonal factors whatever the seasonal specification (package_factor.jl, the three additive cases); the factor of the complete additive polynomial differs, between 0.994 and 1.039 at T = 200 over random invertible draws (check_ma_normalization.py). LIMITATIONS.md, item 22.
